paragraphs: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda, brother of Rabbi Yehudah bar Zavda (see below, Rava b.Z.), Rav Huna’s student. He became sterile as a result of Rav Huna’s lecture, and had no children, Yevamot 64b. (“Rav Acha b.Z.” there is a scribal error, uncorrected in the new Talmud editions.) His colleagues were Rav Sheshet, Rav Giddel, and Rabbi Acha bar Yaakov (see there). He sent Mari bar Mar to ask Rav Huna. Meanwhile Rav Huna died; his son Rabbah told him, “Thus said my father” (see there), Bava Kamma 21, beginning of a. Rabbi Ba bar Zavdi, Rabbi Abbahu, in Rabbi Lazar’s name: the law follows Rabbi Yehudah in the Mishnah. Rabbi Ba b.Z. was praised (they praised and lauded Rabbi Abba) for reporting a teaching from someone younger than himself, Jerusalem Talmud, Sanhedrin, chapter 3, halakhah 6. Rabbi Abba b.Z. said in Rav’s name, Berakhot 11a, 16b; Shabbat 120a, 111, end of a; Sukkah 25a–b—many things; Bava Metzia 25b, 37b; Ketubbot 7a. She'erit Yosef therefore counts him among Rav’s students, by the rule that one who speaks in Rav’s name is his student. But I saw in Jerusalem Talmud, first chapter of Shabbat, on “A person should not sit before the barber,” and at the end of chapter Shemonah Sheratzim: Rabbi Ze'ira asked Rabbi Ba bar Zavdi, “Does the master know Rav, that you report a teaching in his name?” He answered, “Rav Adda bar Ahavah told them in his name.” Thus he expressly did not know Rav and was not Rav’s student. Although I saw at the end of chapter 2 of Shekalim the reading that Rabbi Ze'ira asked Rav Assi, “Do you know Rav?”, etc., and he answered that Rav Adda bar Ahavah told them in his name, I think this a scribal error, since both places above read that Rabbi Zeira asked Rabbi Abba b.Z. Moreover, Rav Assi is known to have been Rav’s student: how could he say that Rav Adda bar Ahavah told him in his name? Yet examination is required: Jerusalem Talmud, chapter Ellu Metzi'ot, halakhah 4, has Rabbi Ba bar Zavdi finding a ḥamra [חמרא; object identification uncertain], going and asking Rav, who told him, “You have not done well,” etc. Thus he did know Rav. In Shabbat 19, end of b, “Rabbah bar Zavda” is a scribal error and should be Rabbi Abba; the same matter appears in Shabbat 120a. Rabbi Tanchuma in Rabbi Chiyya bar Menachema’s name; some say Rabbi Berekhiah bar Chelbo in Rava bar Zavdi’s name, Rabbah, Bechukkotai, end of section 36—certainly a scribal error. He asked Rabbi Abba, first chapter of Megillah; asked Rabbi Abba bar Avina; and Rabbi Abba bar Zutra; and Rabbi Abba bar Mammal. Rav Adda bar Ahavah (see above). He told Rabbi Elazar, “Master, that was not how it happened.” He applied to him, “Two are better than one,” Megillah 5, beginning of b. Rabbi Gamliel Zuga asked him; examination is required there. Rabbi Ze'ira (see above). Rav Huna said in Rabbi Abba b.Z.’s name, Ketubbot 7a: although he was his student, he spoke in his name. Rabbi Chaggai in his name, and he asked him. In R. Chunya of Beit Chavran’s name. He said in Rabbi Chanina’s name, Chullin 19; Kiddushin 75b. He and Rabbi Yoshiyah went out for a fast. He said in Rav Yehudah’s name in Rav’s name, Yevamot 83b. In Rabbi Yitzchak Chakula’s name, Jerusalem Talmud, chapter Get Pashut; Rabbi Yitzchak Chakula in Rabbi Yehudah Nesia’s name. Rabbi Levi Tzenavrayya asked him. He sent Mari bar Mar (see above). Rabbi Simon bar Zavdi—perhaps his brother (see there). He said in Rav’s name (see above). Rava and Rami bar Chama challenged one another. Rabbi Shmuel bar Yehudah in his name; in Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta’s name, Shekalim, chapter 4; in Resh Lakish’s name, Shevi'it, chapter 2. Rav Sheshet (see above). He and Rabbi Tanchum bar Ilai went out for a fast.
